images.title: Jumps that grow
images.purpose: Show the totals 2, 5, 9, 14, 20 whose jumps 3, 4, 5, 6 each grow by 1, so the next jump is 7.
images.composition: Two rows stacked with wide space: the totals on top, the jumps below, centred.
images.exact_structure: Top row: five equal boxes holding 2, 5, 9, 14, 20 in teal #0072B2, evenly spaced. Below, each centred under the gap it describes, four small circles holding +3, +4, +5, +6 in amber #E69F00. Then a fifth circle holding +7 outlined in reddish purple #CC79A7 after the last box. Exactly 5 boxes, 5 circles.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
jumps that are all the same
circles not centred under the gaps
images.takeaway: When the jumps grow by 1 each time, the next jump is one bigger.
images.description: Boxes 2, 5, 9, 14, 20 with growing jumps +3 to +6 below and +7 next.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to read the jumps left to right and say how each differs from the last.

image_decisions.why: Seeing the jumps in their own row makes the growing-by-1 idea clear.
